source_text:
Ὥσπερ οὖν ὁ κύριος ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς οὐδὲν ἐποίησεν, ἡνωμένος ὤν, οὔτε δἰ ἑαυτοῦ οὔτε διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων: οὕτως μηδὲ ὑμεῖς ἄνευ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων μηδὲν πράσσετε: μηδὲ πειράσητε εὔλογόν τι φαίνεσθαι ἰδίᾳ ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ μία προσευχή, μία δέησις, εἷς νοῦς, μία ἐλπὶς ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ἐν τῇ χαρᾷ τῇ ἀμώμῳ, ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὖ ἄμεινον οὐδέν ἐστιν.
πάντες ὡς εἰς ἕνα ναὸν συντρέχετε θεοῦ, ὡς ἐπὶ ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ἐπὶ ἕνα Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν ἀφ̓ ἑνὸς πατρὸς προελθόντα καὶ εἰς ἕνα ὄντα καὶ χωρήσαντα.
thought_title: Do nothing apart from the bishop, as the Lord did nothing apart from the Father
orientation: Ignatius is addressing the Magnesians, urging them to act only in unity with their bishop and elders, just as the Lord acted only in unity with the Father.
pass_a_gloss: Just as therefore the Lord without the Father nothing did, being united, neither by himself nor through the apostles: so neither you without the bishop and the council of elders nothing do: nor try [anything] reasonable to seem privately to you, but in the same [place] one prayer, one supplication, one mind, one hope in love, in the joy the blameless, which is Jesus Christ, than whom better nothing is. All as into one temple run together of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ, the [one] from one Father having come forth and to one being and having returned.

choices.why: Keeps the participial force of the Greek, showing the Lord's unity with the Father as the ground of his action.

choices.term: μηδὲ πειράσητε εὔλογόν τι φαίνεσθαι ἰδίᾳ ὑμῖν
choices.english: do not even try to make anything appear reasonable to you privately
choices.why: Preserves the negative command, the infinitive 'to appear', and the dative 'to you' with 'privately', matching the Greek construction closely.
rejected: do not attempt to seem reasonable on your own
do not try to appear sensible by yourselves

choices.why: Renders the idiomatic phrase literally as a locative expression, which the following list of 'one' items qualifies.
Keeps the article and adjective order of the Greek, emphasizing the joy as a specific, blameless one identified with Christ.
rejected: in the joy that is without blame

choices.english: to one being and having returned
choices.why: Renders the participles literally: 'being' (ὄντα) and 'having returned' (χωρήσαντα), preserving the movement from and to the Father.
rejected: and was with one and returned to one
to the one who is and has gone

pass_b_english: The Lord was united with the Father, and so he did nothing without the Father, neither by himself nor through the apostles. In the same way, you must do nothing without the bishop and the council of elders. Do not even try to make anything appear reasonable to you privately. Instead, gather together in one place and have one prayer, one supplication, one mind, one hope in love, in the blameless joy, which is Jesus Christ, than whom nothing is better.
All of you, run together as into one temple of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ, who came forth from one Father and is one and has returned to him.

problems.why: χωρήσαντα means 'containing, receiving, holding' or 'having room for', not 'returned'. The sense is Christ who 'contains' or 'embraces' all, or 'has returned' is wrong.
problems.fix: who came forth from one Father and remains one and embraces all
problems.ruling: χωρήσαντα means 'departed/withdrawn' or 'contained'; 'returned' misrepresents the final clause about Christ's procession and unity.

edits.old: who came forth from one Father and is in one and has returned.
edits.new: who came forth from one Father and is in one and embraces all.

problems.quote: is in one and embraces all
problems.why: Misreads εἰς ἕνα ὄντα ('existing as one'/'being one') as 'is in one'; changes meaning from Christ's unity to location.
problems.fix: who came forth from one Father and is one and embraces all

edits.old: who came forth from one Father and is in one and embraces all
edits.new: who came forth from one Father and is one and embraces all

fixed: Changed 'is in one' to 'is one' to match the source's 'εἰς ἕνα ὄντα' (being one).

problems.why: Same Greek presbyterion rendered with and without parenthetical 'presbyters', risking confusion.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note.

problems.quote: council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
problems.why: Same word 'council' used for presbyterion and apostolic group, but different Greek words may be involved; still risks conflation.
problems.fix: Note Greek terms or use 'college of apostles' if distinct.

edits.old: who came forth from one Father and is one and embraces all.
edits.new: who came forth from one Father and is in one and has returned.

fixed: The glossary problems are not about the English translation but about the literal gloss and terminology consistency. The English already uses 'council of elders' consistently for πρεσβυτέριον, and the second flagged item refers to the literal gloss, not the English. No change needed in the English translation for these.

The edit to 'who came forth from one Father and is in one and has returned' was previously tried and rejected, but re-reading the source shows the Greek 'εἰς ἕνα ὄντα καὶ χωρήσαντα' means 'being in one and having returned', so the current English 'is one and embraces all' is inaccurate. The correct rendering is 'is in one and has returned'.

problems.why: 'Council of elders' is standard, but 'council of the apostles' and 'council of the bishop' appear once each, potentially confusing the structure.
problems.fix: Clarify if these are the same body or different.

edits.old: who came forth from one Father and is in one and has returned.
edits.new: who came forth from one Father and is in one and has returned to him.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'council of elders' is not a translation error in this passage; the English already uses the standard glossary term correctly.

problems.why: 'Council of elders' is standard, but 'council of the apostles' and 'council of the bishop' appear once each; reader may miss these are the same institution.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note where source differs.

problems.why: Same Greek term (thysiastērion) rendered inconsistently with/without article; not serious but worth noting.

problems.quote: who came forth from one Father and is in one and has returned to him
problems.why: 'Is in one' is ungrammatical and unclear; 'one' what?
problems.fix: Likely 'is one' or 'is in unity'; rephrase: 'who came from the one Father and is one with him and has returned to him.'

edits.old: who came forth from one Father and is in one and has returned to him
edits.new: who came forth from one Father and is one and has returned to him

fixed: The source reads 'εἰς ἕνα ὄντα' (to one being), which means 'is one' or 'is in unity with the Father', not 'is in one'. The English 'is in one' is ungrammatical and unclear. Changed to 'is one' to match the source's 'εἰς ἕνα ὄντα'.
The glossary problems about 'council of elders' and 'altar' are not actual translation errors in this section; the English uses the standard glossary terms correctly. No edit needed.

polish.changed: Clarified that the Lord's unity with the Father is the model for the church's unity under the bishop and elders, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
notes.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

notes.quote: council of elders of the church

variants.text: council of elders of the church

notes.why: Same entity as 'council of elders' elsewhere; 'of the church' adds no distinction but may confuse.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening comparison by making the Lord the explicit subject, replaced the archaic 'let there be' with a direct command to gather and have one prayer, and smoothed the sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: 'Council of elders' vs plain 'elders' may seem different institutions; 'council of the apostles' is analogical.
notes.fix: Consistently use 'council of elders' or note equivalence.
